restrictions: Two distinct 64-byte messages M(x), M(y). W0..W7 are the fixed prefix in proof Section 1. W8=y0, W9=y1, and W10..W15 are y2..y7 minus K10..K15 modulo 2^32. This is a bijection from the 256-bit chain value x. FIPS padding adds one fixed second block. The target uses the standard IV, steps 0..47 on each block, and feed-forward. The walk g is an explicitly invertible encoding of the block-1 working state (walk B with tail shear masks QM=0x7c350f64 and XM=0x1d223aa4) XOR the fixed polarity mask 7fd81be44b62b302c8d9beea0c8abe43ab19e0d125a729edaf14e9c82d847324. A collision of g gives equal complete digests.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5, C=3568. The declared machine has 874 256-bit registers, 871 data and three pointers. Every XOR, AND, OR, NOT, move, set, load, store, addition, comparison, branch, and random word is charged. Its native body instruction is exactly 32 bits: a 2-bit opcode and three 10-bit register fields, fetched and executed directly at one operation per instruction under the same pricing convention as the accepted native 5-byte format. No decoder or interpreter runs in the normative path; Prog.run, Prog.compile, and Prog.fast are test-only mirrors. Recovery and control use native fixed 5-byte instructions. The kernel has 57637 instructions (45234 XOR, 7611 AND, 4792 OR); stage 1 and loop control add 22 and 3 operations per batch.

The single attempt uses one fresh uniform r, no restart, no amplification, no stored collision, and no advice. Distinguished points have low 20 bits zero and the next 102 bits below 1959. The table stores 126879 completed trails in 127142 trail-index slots. Each 48-bit slot stores key+1; zero is the empty sentinel, and the slot position is the trail number. Recovery recomputes the stored trail length and uses the 420-record rolled program (92 one-time initialization records), executing 1819 records per call plus at most 76 itemized surrounding operations, including 10 per-call register re-sets.

Exact ledger: B=1324645323083147000000000000000000000, c=35283234191330079321591611605195467, and N=76517233115733222172580812912278110293151 word operations. log2(N/3568)=124.012008601951. The claim rounds upward to 124.01201. Final setup and emission cost 237921609 operations. The 1641-evaluation offset search costs 461900436782186496 operations. The reserved 579-evaluation selector-validation envelope costs 162974011515469824 operations. All are included in N and preprocessing_log2.

Search memory is 238808 bytes of code, 762852 bytes of table, 16384 bytes of counters and copies, 27968 bytes of registers, and 2560 bytes of recovery arrays: 1048572 bytes. Normative setup adds a 340740-byte wasm emitter image and 92684 bytes of itemized scratch to the final code, counters, registers, and recovery arrays: 719144 bytes. The sequential preprocessing searches peak below setup. Search is the overall peak. The self-test asserts every body, control, key, and trail field boundary.

For a uniformly random 256-bit function, proof Section 4 and Appendix A give P_F at least 0.390000001000 using exact integers and outward-rounded 60-digit decimals. H1 is the score-critical comparison that transfers this bound to the fixed reduced-round SHA-256 walk. Proof Section 5 states its support, scope, and exact sensitivity.

The freestanding C source embedded as GEN_C (SHA-256 1c9f5d9efda6532fdf513bb35bdcb01072de0c6527018d4b59f2d5ddaad1d95f) is the normative setup emitter. Compiled to wasm32 with the stated wasi-sdk 25 clang 19.1.5 flags, its exported run function executes exactly 118554004 participant-measured wasm operators (Wasmtime 26.0.0 fuel) and emits 57637 instructions. Before every declared experiment, the byte-exact Python BoundedEmitter mirror checks all 15 C fields, the C source hash, stream hash 94c63bd2fdc64494fe64202c0b8313e490305dc38c94fe6a56d5f16ec7b2cdbb, polarity mask, bounds, and ordinary-builder equality. Circuit optimizations are exact equivalences checked by the self-test; they are not premises.

The declared organizer experiments are consistency checks. bssha-n16 performs one width-16 search attempt per trial. proj-k0-w256 evaluates 256 full-width points and forms the complete two-block 48-step digest. The organizer recomputes every returned event. No experiment count changes the score.

heuristics.statement: Model premise with four explicit clauses. Let F be a uniformly random function from 256-bit values to 256-bit values and let A_F be this exact bounded attempt with every call to the fixed walk g replaced by lazy sampling from F. H1 states that the real attempt succeeds at least as often as A_F. (a) Distinct fresh evaluated inputs have independent uniform outputs and pair-collision hazard 2^-256. (b) Iterates from the starts r+t have the first-collision law of a random mapping. (c) A fresh output is distinguished with probability 1959/2^122 independently of collision events. (d) Under the program's adaptive choices, given the complete earlier history and the later DP flags, a fresh output equals any fixed earlier non-DP output with probability at least 2^-256. Proof Section 4 proves P_F >= 0.390000001000 for F, and Section 5 states the support and sensitivity of the fixed-target comparison.
heuristics.scope: The fixed target sha256-r48-prefix-v1 restricted to the 64-byte message family of proof Section 1, one attempt of B=1324645323083147000000000000000000000 batches and Q=339109202709285632000000000000000000000 evaluations, about 124943.75 trails of mean length 5316911983139663491615228241121378304/1959 = 2^111.0641, with 256 trails advanced together. It is not claimed for other messages, rounds, or scales.
heuristics.extrapolation: Support of H1 is stated in proof Section 5. (1) H1 is the generic premise of parallel collision search with distinguished points: Paul C. van Oorschot and Michael J. Wiener, 'Parallel Collision Search with Cryptanalytic Applications', Journal of Cryptology 12(1):1-28, 1999, DOI 10.1007/PL00003816, model a fixed compression function iterated from fresh starts, without a chosen input difference, by a random function. The generic entries of this track use the same premise, including the round-64 entries 7523902c and c9ae3732 and the previous best round-48 entry a4d3505b. (2) Clause (d) fails adversely only if g, along its own iterates, collides less often than a random function by a factor 1-eps. Such a property would separate this 48-step SHA-256 walk from a random function in a way no published result shows; this entry chooses no input difference and uses no differential property. (3) A higher hazard helps. Replanning a deficit costs 0.00725035 bit at eps=0.01 (Tp 1949), 0.03700268 at eps=0.05 (Tp 1909), 0.07600609 at eps=0.10 (Tp 1858), and 0.20753071 at eps=0.25 (Tp 1696). (4) The program checks agree with random-function references at their scopes: proj-k0-w256 expects 100.53 of 256 trials with a pair; bssha-n16 expects 178.14 of 256 (exact-plan lazy-random-function reference, 10000000 mappings, probability 0.6958435, standard error 0.00014548). A participant-run replay with substitute seeds returned 105 and 198, every pair recomputed with the verifier digest. These counts are consistency checks, not inputs to the score.
heuristics.limitations: H1 cannot be tested at width 256: the experiments reach the complete search at width 16 and 16-bit projections of 256 full-width points, so they cannot measure the full-width collision hazard or the success probability at 2^128 scale. The exact sensitivity costs above restore 0.39 under specified hazard deficits. Circuit equivalences, instruction counts, memory bounds, and the theorem for F do not depend on H1.
